subject: Renewal runway diagnostic — layered buffer proposal
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Lombardi <peter.lombardi@pioneerhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal runway diagnostic — layered buffer proposal

Hi Peter,

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our renewal conversation I pulled a short diagnostic and sketched three practical sizing paths based on your trailing-90d utilization and expected product launch spikes. Attached is the workbook (runway_diagnostic_q2.xlsx) with a day-by-day simulated GPU-hour burn and sensitivity to average seq length / batch size.

High-level options (numbers are incremental GPUs above your committed base of 24 H100s):
- Conservative buffer (short runway risk): +6 GPUs; keeps unit cost low but limited burst headroom.
- Balanced (recommended): +12 GPUs with burst capacity and autoscale policy; 60-day evaluation window to re-sync commit.
- Aggressive safety index: +20 GPUs; minimizes throttling risk for peak new-model launches.

We recommend the Balanced option with a staged onboarding: enable burst capacity, set a conservative autoscale ceiling for the first 30 days, and then re-evaluate telemetry (KV cache hit, tail latency, percent tokens served from cache). I've attached a one-page mutual_action_plan.md that maps milestones and acceptance criteria.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow (Jun 29) to walk through the workbook and nail down preferred option? If you want, we can include procurement on the call so we can confirm PO timing.

Best,
Irene

--
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0128

(attachment: runway_diagnostic_q2.xlsx)

From: Peter Lombardi <peter.lombardi@pioneerhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-28T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal runway diagnostic — layered buffer proposal

Thanks Irene — this is helpful. Quick questions before we jump on a call:

1) How did you model the new model launch? Our engineering team expects a 3x spike for ~36 hours per release cycle but average load otherwise.
2) Is the +12 balanced option prescriptive or flexible? We'd prefer a path that starts smaller and scales if the release generates sustained usage.

Also looping in procurement: Susan Lee (susan.lee@pioneerhealth.com) — she will handle PO timing and billing questions.

If you can show a phased path (minimal up-front commit + canary burst + automatic re-eval) we'll be in a good place. Call tomorrow afternoon works.

Peter
Director of ML Platforms
Pioneer Health

Date: 2026-06-28T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal runway diagnostic — layered buffer proposal (Pioneer Health)

Team — forwarding Peter's note. He explicitly asked for a phased path: minimal up-front, canary burst for releases, automatic re-eval at 60 days, and procurement in the loop.

Proposed operational plan for sales/procurement + SE/ops alignment: 
- Phase 0 (prep): confirm burst pool configuration and quota bump window; set alerts for cache hit < 40% and 95th pct latency > target.
- Phase 1 (canary): +6 GPUs as burst ceiling for release windows for 30 days; telemetry gated (KV hit rate, token/sec, tail latency).
- Phase 2 (commit review): after 30 days, if utilization > 70% of balanced option for 7 consecutive days, recommend converting to +12 commit with 60-day SLA credit for early conversion.
- Fallback: if severe tail latency or error rate rises above thresholds, automatic rollback to base pool and temporary burst disablement while we remediate.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.md (one-pager), and I'm attaching the runway workbook for reference. Karthik — can you confirm the technical feasibility of the autoscale ceilings and the recommended alert thresholds? Ben/Vanessa — any commercial constraints we should call out for permitting a short-term commit conversion path?

Irene

(attachment: mutual_action_plan.md, runway_diagnostic_q2.xlsx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-28T13:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal runway diagnostic — layered buffer proposal (Pioneer Health)

Quick notes from SE perspective — feasible with existing Dedicated config and autoscale policy. Key points: 

- Autoscale ceiling: we can expose a 'burst ceiling' that is non-committing (i.e., paid at on-demand rates until converted). Good for the canary approach.
- Suggested alert thresholds: KV cache hit < 45% (investigate prompt engineering/caching); 95th pct request latency > 350ms (for H100 profile) to trigger investigation; sustained GPU utilization > 78% for 7 days to recommend commit.
- Forecast snippet (see attached util_forecast_model_v3.csv): with a 3x 36-hour release spike every two weeks, expected additional GPU-hours over 30 days = ~3,900 GPU-hours (balanced scenario). That maps to ~8 extra H100s if spikes coincide with steady-state increases.

Operational asks: we will need a signed MAA for burst caps > +10 GPUs (security/ops gating) and 72h lead time for provisioning if they choose aggressive +20 path.

I'll drop by the call tomorrow.

—Karthik
Lead Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
(karthik_iyer@redwood.ai)

(attachment: util_forecast_model_v3.csv)

From: Peter Lombardi <peter.lombardi@pioneerhealth.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-28T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal runway diagnostic — layered buffer proposal

Thanks — that approach aligns with what we had in mind. Let's go with the phased plan:

- Start with Phase 1 canary: enable +6 GPU burst ceiling, have Karthik's alerts configured, and run for 30 days.
- If telemetry meets the commit trigger (sustained >78% utilization per Karthik), convert to balanced +12 commit with a 60-day evaluation window.
- Procurement note: Susan, please advise on PO cadence. We'd prefer the flexibility to convert after the canary without a full upfront 12-month long-term commitment; if necessary we can do a 90-day convertible commit.

One ask: if we convert to +12 within 60 days, can Redwood offer a 10% first-year credit on the delta commit as an incentive? That will help sell this internally — reduces our short-term cash impact.

Irene/Karthik — please prepare a simple SOW and the convertible commit language for procurement. We'll aim to get a PO within 10 business days pending final SOW.

Peter
